name: Gato Negro

waypoints.name: SR-20 Wine Spires / Silver Star pullout (~MP 165, ~4 mi east of Washington Pass)
waypoints.note: Climbers park at this pullout, descend to and cross Early Winters Creek, then climb a steep climbers trail to the Bench (~6,500-6,700ft) below Burgundy Col, from which all Wine Spires routes (including Whine Spire/Gato Negro) and Silver Star's standard route are reached.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to the unsigned Wine Spires / Silver Star pullout east of Washington Pass, near milepost 165-166 and roughly 4 miles past the pass, at about 4,300 to 4,400 feet. It is a plain roadside pull-off with no sign and no developed parking, so watch your mileposts. Do not confuse it with the Blue Lake trailhead, which is on the other side of Washington Pass entirely.

waypoints.name: Whine Spire (Gato Negro topout)
waypoints.note: 12-pitch alpine trad route (sustained 5.10a/b with a 5.10d crux) on the sub-peak east of Silver Star Mountain; topout elevation is approximate.

waypoints.name: Whine Spire summit (sub-peak on Silver Star Mountain's ridge, east side)

approach: From the pullout, find a faint boot path descending loose talus/scree to the east into the trees, passing a trail register, then crossing Early Winters Creek on a log (~4,080 ft). The trail climbs the timbered rib north of Burgundy Creek, steeply gaining elevation to a basin/camp bench around 6,500 ft (roughly 2 hours from the car), then continues up to Burgundy Col (~7,720 ft, ~3 hours). Whine Spire, just south of the Wine Spires, is reached from the col; good camping and a late-season spring are near 6,400-6,500 ft.

approach_variants.name: Burgundy Col to the east side of Silver Star's ridge
approach_variants.notes: Whine Spire is a sub-peak on the east side of Silver Star Mountain's ridge, below and south of the line of Wine Spires, and its east face is reached from the far side of Burgundy Col. From the pullout on SR-20 a few miles east of Washington Pass, take the boot path down to Early Winters Creek, cross on the log near 4,080 ft, and climb the timbered rib north of Burgundy Creek to the bench camp near 6,500 ft, then on to the col. Drop off the east side and traverse south beneath the east faces. Expect a patch of steep snow on that traverse and, later in the season, awkward scree-filled moats where the snow has pulled back from the rock.
hazards: Steep snow patch and scree-filled moats on the traverse in to the base
A 5.9+ offwidth chimney section high on the route
Twelve long pitches, most 180 ft or more — a full day for most parties
approach_variants.baseFinding: The hand crack, not the chimney — that is the one decision at the bottom. Standing under the east face of Whine Spire there are two plausible starts within a few metres of each other. Around the corner and to the right is a clean, blocky chimney that looks better than it is, and the route deliberately avoids it. The climb proper begins to its left on a steep crack that gives finger locks and solid hand jams straight off the ground and never narrows into a chimney or a squeeze. Commit only when the feature above you is a crack you can jam, set in a face rather than tucked in a corner. Late in the season a scree-choked moat sits between the snow and the rock at the base: cross it and rack up on the rock, because there is nowhere flat to sort gear once you have stepped across.

overview: Gato Negro is a newer alpine rock route on the East Face of Silver Star Mountain's sub-peak Whine Spire. This big, sustained 1,500-foot climb features impressive granite pitches with mostly solid rock, though loose sections and tricky route-finding require careful attention.
